governments.name: Democracy
governments.summary: Strong economy. Offensive wars hurt stability unless war support is high.

governments.name: Constitutional Monarchy
governments.summary: The steadiest system. A head of state above politics.

governments.name: One-Party State
governments.summary: Mobilises people easily. Free nations trust it less.

governments.name: Military Government
governments.summary: Cheap, fast armies. Weak economy and shaky stability.

units.name: Infantry
units.description: Sixty riflemen with machine guns and anti-tank launchers. Cheap, everywhere, and the only unit that can wade across water on its own.
bestUsedFor: Soaking up an attack behind defences

units.name: Special Forces
units.description: A dozen elite operators trained for sabotage, raids and deep reconnaissance. Light, quiet and dangerous behind the lines.
bestUsedFor: Spotting ahead of the main force

units.name: Scout
units.description: A small mounted patrol that sees further than it can fight. Fast enough to find the enemy and get away again.
bestUsedFor: Pushing back the fog of war

units.name: Light Tank
units.description: A fast, lightly armoured tank. Hits harder than infantry and moves quicker than a main battle tank, but can't trade blows with one.

units.name: Main Battle Tank
units.description: Heavy armour and a big gun. The backbone of any land offensive, but slow, thirsty and hungry for ammunition.
bestUsedFor: Spearheading with supply trucks close behind

units.name: SP Artillery
units.description: A self-propelled howitzer. Fires on cells up to two away without ever entering the fight, but its thin armour means it must stay behind the line.
bestUsedFor: Shelling a contested cell before you assault
Wearing down an attack on your own lines
units.weakAgainst: Anything that reaches it: tanks, aircraft

units.name: Mobile Radar
units.description: A truck-mounted search radar. Sees aircraft and movement far over the horizon and gives nearby air defence something to aim at.
bestUsedFor: Extending your vision over a front

units.name: Helicopter
units.description: An attack helicopter armed with anti-tank missiles and cannon. Strikes cells up to two away and is a menace to armour and small ships.

units.name: Jet Fighter
units.description: A multi-role fighter. Rules the sky, then turns its missiles and bombs on anything within three cells.
bestUsedFor: Air strikes deep behind the front

units.name: Airborne Radar
units.description: A flying radar station. Unarmed, but it sees four cells in every direction and spots what everything else misses.
units.weakAgainst: Jets; keep it behind your own fighters

units.name: Frigate
units.description: A general-purpose warship with guns, missiles and sonar. Shells targets on the coast and hunts submarines.
units.weakAgainst: Submarines that strike first, massed jets

units.name: Submarine
units.description: A hunter-killer submarine. Invisible without sonar, and its torpedoes sink almost anything that floats.
bestUsedFor: Escorting your own convoys from below

units.name: Radar Picket
units.description: A radar picket ship bristling with anti-air missiles. Sees far and swats aircraft out of the sky one cell around it.
bestUsedFor: Shooting down air strikes on the coast

units.name: Transport Truck
units.description: An army truck for moving foot soldiers fast along roads. Unarmed: lose it and the passengers spill out hurt.
bestUsedFor: Moving infantry up to the front

units.name: Transport Aircraft
units.description: A heavy airlifter. Flies troops and light vehicles anywhere in range and drops paratroopers onto enemy ground.
bestUsedFor: Carrying light tanks and radar to airbases
units.weakAgainst: Jets and air defence; cargo dies with it

units.name: Transport Ship
units.description: A roll-on roll-off transport ship. Carries a small army, tanks included, across the water and lands it on a coast.
bestUsedFor: Ferrying supply trucks to a new front

units.name: Supply Truck
units.description: A fuel and ammunition truck. Refills every friendly unit in its own cell and the cells next door, running supplies forward to the front.
bestUsedFor: Keeping tanks moving deep in enemy land
Resupplying a fight from one cell back
units.weakAgainst: Raiders; keep it attached or one cell back

units.name: Supply Aircraft
units.description: An aerial tanker and cargo plane. Resupplies units up to two cells away, over land or sea.

units.name: Supply Ship
units.description: A fleet oiler. Refuels and rearms ships and coastal units in its own and neighbouring cells.

battalions.name: Armoured Battalion
battalions.requirement: 3+ tanks (main battle or light), at most 1 infantry

battalions.name: Mechanised Battalion
battalions.effect: Combined arms: hits 10% harder and takes 8% less damage.

battalions.name: Infantry Battalion
battalions.effect: Dug in: takes 15% less damage holding friendly ground.

battalions.name: Special Operations Group
battalions.requirement: Special forces plus scouts or more special forces
battalions.effect: Raiders: 30% more damage to support units and structures.

battalions.name: Strike Wing
battalions.effect: Coordinated sorties: strikes 15% stronger, 20% less damage from air defence.

battalions.name: Naval Task Force
battalions.effect: Layered defences: ships take 12% less damage.

battalions.name: Amphibious Group
battalions.requirement: A transport ship plus a warship

battalions.name: Supply Convoy
battalions.requirement: A supply unit plus an escort or more supply
battalions.effect: Supplies transfer in a single turn alongside.

buildings.name: Airbase
buildings.purpose: A runway with hangars and a control tower: the home of your air force.
buildings.placement: Any land cell you hold. Aircraft can only be recruited at an airbase in a city or capital of your own country, not on captured ground.
buildings.howItWorks: One level. Aircraft based here are fully refuelled and rearmed each turn (a logistics depot does the same). The airbase has no guns of its own: anti-air fire comes only from units in the cell.
tips: Station anti-air capable units with your aircraft to defend the base.
Aircraft return to their home base when fuel runs low, so build bases near the fronts you'll fight over.
Airbases are prime strike targets: losing one strands the aircraft that use it.

levels.effect: Aircraft can be recruited here (home cities only); aircraft here are refuelled and rearmed

buildings.name: Defences
buildings.purpose: Fortified positions: bunkers, trenches and wire that shield your land units from enemy fire.
buildings.placement: Any land cell you hold. One construction at a time per cell.
buildings.howItWorks: Protects land units friendly to the cell's owner, against both direct fire and bombardment. It doesn't protect ships, aircraft or attackers standing in the cell. Capturing the cell destroys one level, and strikes can wreck levels.
tips: Fortify capitals and border cities first: they hold the most victory points.
Defences multiply with terrain cover, so jungle and urban cells become very hard to take.
Pair with artillery behind the line to punish attackers stuck in front of the wall.

buildings.name: Factory
buildings.purpose: An industrial complex producing both money and materials.
buildings.placement: Any land cell you hold; best in cities you're unlikely to lose.
buildings.howItWorks: Its output joins your economy each turn. Funds are scaled by your government and stability and halved on occupied land. Materials are only scaled by your economic policy (free market 90%, state-directed 120%) and aren't reduced on occupied land.
tips: Factories are the main source of materials for most nations.
Upgrade a few factories deep rather than many shallow ones: the cost per level rises slowly.
Keep them behind the front: strikes and capture take levels away.

buildings.name: Logistics depot
buildings.purpose: Storage and supply infrastructure that keeps armies fuelled and armed.
buildings.howItWorks: Gives full resupply of fuel and ammunition in its cell and the adjacent cells, two cells out from level 3. Supply columns (trucks, supply aircraft and supply ships) standing in the depot's own cell reload faster with each level. Resupply is paid from your national fuel and materials.
tips: Build depots just behind the front so attacking units refill every turn.
Level 3 is the big step: the supply area grows to two cells.
Combine with supply trucks to reach units beyond the depot's area.

buildings.name: Military Training Centre
buildings.purpose: Military training grounds that prepare recruits for deployment faster.
buildings.howItWorks: Each level adds to national manpower growth, counted across all your centres up to the cap. It's added to the hospital bonus rather than multiplied, and it raises your reserve ceiling too.
tips: Spread centres across your cities or concentrate them: only the total level counts, up to +25%.
Build them early in a long war: the extra manpower adds up over many turns.
A captured centre works for the enemy, so build them in secure cities.

buildings.name: Hospital
buildings.purpose: A military hospital that heals units in its cell and returns more of your people to service.
buildings.howItWorks: Healing in the cell runs once a turn and draws manpower (1% of the unit's manpower cost per health point). The manpower bonus counts every hospital level across all land you hold, up to the cap.
tips: Put hospitals where your armies regroup: a level-5 hospital heals 20 health a turn.
Several level-1 hospitals give the same manpower bonus as one big one, but healing only happens in the hospital's own cell.
Healing costs manpower, so watch your reserve during long wars.

buildings.name: Mine
buildings.purpose: An extraction site that digs raw industrial materials from an ore deposit.
buildings.placement: Only on a land cell with an ore deposit.
buildings.howItWorks: An ore cell already gives +1.5 materials without a mine; the mine adds its own output on top. Like all materials, the total is scaled by your economic policy. Output isn't reduced if the cell is occupied, so a captured mine works for its new owner.
tips: Develop every ore deposit you hold: it's the cheapest steady material supply.
Protect mining cells: they're prize targets for invaders.
Materials pay for heavy units and ships, so mines matter most for navies and armour.

buildings.name: Oil well
buildings.purpose: Extraction equipment pumping crude from an oil deposit to fuel your forces.
buildings.placement: Only on a land cell with an oil deposit.
buildings.howItWorks: An oil cell already gives +1.5 fuel without a well. Fuel keeps aircraft flying, ships sailing and tanks moving.
tips: Air forces and navies burn fuel fast; wells keep them operating far from home.
Losing your wells mid-war grounds aircraft, so defend them.
Fuel can also be bought on the market, but wells are cheaper over time.

buildings.name: Offshore oil rig
buildings.purpose: An offshore platform drilling an undersea oil field.
buildings.placement: Only over an offshore oil field in your own territorial waters.
buildings.howItWorks: Fuel goes to whoever owns the waters, so the rig changes hands if the coast does.
tips: Rigs are the only fuel source for many island nations.
Keep warships nearby: an exposed rig is an easy target.
Holding the coastline keeps the rig's output.

buildings.name: Roads
buildings.purpose: Paved roads that speed up land movement and lift the cell's income.
buildings.placement: Any land cell you hold. A road only speeds moves when both cells on the route have roads; the lower level counts.
buildings.howItWorks: Movement uses the road rate for any unit travelling between two road cells, invaders included. The income bonus applies to the cell's own income.
tips: Build chains of roads from your cities to the front so reinforcements arrive in fewer turns.
Battalions move at their slowest unit's pace, so roads matter most for tanks and artillery.
Remember the enemy can drive on your roads too once they break through.

guide.title: Pick a nation and set it up
guide.text: Choose its government and rights, then buy a starting army. Every nation gets the same 240 requisition points to spend. Everyone starts neutral. Win by holding 30% of the Pacific's victory points: capitals 10, cities 3, provinces 1.

guide.title: Give orders
guide.text: Tap a zone with your units, press Order, then tap a destination. Highlighted zones are reached this turn; anything further takes several turns. The dotted route stays until they arrive.

guide.title: Hunt them down
guide.text: Order units onto an enemy you can see and they pursue it: if it moves they follow, ranged units stop as soon as it's in range and open fire, and the hunt ends when it's destroyed, slips into the fog, or your unit falls. Any new order calls the hunt off.

guide.title: End the turn
guide.text: Your orders play out first, then every AI moves. Units that meet enemies fight; land units capture enemy provinces they enter. The camera then follows every significant move and fight: Next jumps to the next event, 2× doubles the speed, Skip ends the replay.

guide.title: Build
guide.text: Tap your own province to add defences, roads, hospitals, factories, mines, oil wells, depots, airbases or (in cities) training centres, and upgrade most of them from level 1 to 5 (an airbase has one level). Recruit in cities: each city and capital can start 4 units a turn, and a unit ordered this turn can be cancelled for a full refund. Soldiers and crews come out of your manpower reserve, and so do reinforcements when damaged units heal.

guide.title: Mind the economy
guide.text: Units cost upkeep in funds and fuel. Buy fuel and materials under Nation → Economy.

guide.title: Use diplomacy
guide.text: Pacts, alliances, aid and envoys shape how leaders treat you. Their personalities shift as the war unfolds.

guide.title: Keep them supplied
guide.text: Every unit carries fuel and ammo. Moving burns fuel, fighting burns ammo. Cities, logistics depots and supply trucks, aircraft and ships refill them. Cut the enemy's supply lines and their tanks stop.

guide.title: Chain of command
guide.text: Attach support units (transports and supply) to a combat unit of the same arm. Order the commander and they follow; enemies must beat the commander before they can touch them. Unattached support can be destroyed, and a sunk or downed transport takes its cargo with it.

guide.title: Fight
guide.text: Units that meet an enemy they're at war with become engaged. At the end of every turn each unit fires once at the best target on its priority list, using its attack values against land, air, ships, subs and structures, its health and ammo, and the target's armour, terrain and defences. Fighting goes on turn after turn until one side is destroyed or pulls out. A land cell with no defending troops left changes hands. Set what each unit shoots first with Targets; the forecast shows what to expect before you commit.

guide.title: Fire from range
guide.text: Artillery (2 cells), jets (4), helicopters (2), frigates and radar pickets (1) can hit a cell without entering it: select them and press Attack. Aircraft draw fire from enemy air defences. Units keep firing every turn until the target is clear or you call them off.

guide.title: Carry troops
guide.text: At a port (or airbase), press Embark to load units onto a transport. Nothing goes ashore by itself: sail into a friendly port and press Disembark, or sit offshore of an enemy coast and press Assault. Every island has at least one port.

guide.title: The sea
guide.text: Lighter water is shallow: big ships move slower there and submarines are easy to find and kill. Deep ocean is where subs hide and hit hardest. Each nation owns the waters around its coast; your aircraft can't cross a neutral nation's airspace, and offshore oil fields in your waters can take a rig. Four great rivers are navigable: the Yangtze up to Wuhan, the Pearl to Guangzhou, the Mekong to Phnom Penh and the Irrawaddy to Mandalay. Ships sail them through friendly river ports, which build transports and supply ships. Ship radar picks up contacts out to its full range, but a ship identifies what it sees only within 1 cell: beyond that, enemies show as red radar contacts.

guide.title: Read the reports
guide.text: After each turn the Fractured Coasts Network covers what you saw clearly, plus rumours from places you can't see.

guide.title: Commander guidance
guide.text: A new campaign can walk you through your first turns. After that, a short lesson appears only when you first meet something: ships, a transport, loading and landing troops, a supply column, a battle. Your next objective, under the resource bar, offers ideas from what you can see; ignore it freely. Guidance never acts for you. Turn either part off, or read any lesson again, under Nation → Commander guidance.

notes.startingArmy: Powers pick their own starting army with 240 points; minor nations' starting forces are fixed.
